'''Brian Martin''' (born 1947) is a social scientist in the School of Humanities and Social Inquiry, Faculty of Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities, at the [[University of Wollongong]] (UOW) in NSW, Australia.<ref name=uow-bm>{{cite web |title=Brian Martin |url=https://scholars.uow.edu.au/display/brian_martin |website=scholars.uow.edu.au |publisher=University of Wollongong Australia |access-date=11 August 2021 |archive-date=25 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210525052351/https://scholars.uow.edu.au/display/brian_martin |url-status=live }}</ref> He was appointed a professor at the university in 2007, and in 2017 was appointed [[Emeritus|emeritus professor]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last1=Raper |first1=Judy |author-link1=Judy Raper |title=Emeritus Professor Brian Martin |url=https://www.uow.edu.au/alumni/honorary-alumni/emeritus/brian-martin/ |date=1 November 2017|publisher=[[University of Wollongong]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622182845/https://www.uow.edu.au/alumni/honorary-alumni/emeritus/brian-martin/|archive-date=22 June 2019}}</ref> His work is in the fields of peace research, scientific controversies, [[science and technology studies]], sociology, political science, media studies, law, journalism, [[freedom of speech]], education and corrupted institutions,<ref name=":2" /><ref name="uow-bm"/><ref name="book review"/> as well as research on [[whistleblowing]] and [[dissent]] in the context of [[science]].<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=http://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/news/opinion/monoculture-is-killing-thought/2008/12/03/1228257139381.html|title=Monoculture is killing thought|last=Devine|first=Miranda|date=4 December 2008|work=[[Brisbane Times]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181122005758/https://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/national/monoculture-is-killing-thought-20081204-gdt59m.html|archive-date=22 November 2018|publisher=Fairfax}}</ref><ref name="delborne2008">{{cite journal |last1=Delborne |first1=Jason A. |title=Transgenes and Transgressions: Scientific Dissent as Heterogeneous Practice |journal=[[Social Studies of Science]] |year= 2008 |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=509–541 |doi=10.1177/0306312708089716|jstor=25474595|pmid=19227618 |s2cid=10272587 }}</ref> Martin was president of Whistleblowers Australia from 1996 to 1999 and remains their International Director.<ref name="abc-perspective">{{cite news|last=Barclay|first=Paul|url=http://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/perspective/dr-brian-martin/3412188|title=Perspective: Whistleblowers and Iraq|date=10 May 2004|work=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC Radio]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207234202/https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/archived/perspective/dr-brian-martin/3412188|archive-date=7 February 2020}}</ref> He has been criticized by medical professionals and public health advocates for promoting the disproven [[oral polio vaccine AIDS hypothesis]] and supporting [[vaccine hesitancy]] in the context of his work.<ref name="Australian-spruik" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Jenkins |first=Stephen H. |title=Tools for Critical Thinking in Biology |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2015 |isbn=978-0-19-998104-5 |location=New York |pages=217–219 |oclc=904046627 |quote=Although Hooper and Martin are still promoting the tainted polio vaccine hypothesis, recent genetic work has convincingly disproven it... Worobey's team published their genetic comparison of HIV samples in 2008, but Brian Martin continued to promote the tainted polio vaccine hypothesis for the origin of AIDS as late as 2010 in a paper called "How to Attack a Scientific Theory and Get Away with It (Usually)..."}}</ref><ref name="australian-conference"/>

Martin has spoken at a [[British Science Association]] Festival of Science,<ref name="BBC">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/in_depth/sci_tech/2000/festival_of_science/919572.stm|title=Science needs its whistleblowers|last=Murcott|first=Toby|date=11 September 2000|work=[[BBC News]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170828150511/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/in_depth/sci_tech/2000/festival_of_science/919572.stm|archive-date=28 August 2017}}</ref> and testified at the [[Australian Senate|Australian Federal Senate's]] Inquiry into Academic Freedom.<ref name=":0"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Committees/Senate/Education_Employment_and_Workplace_Relations/Completed_inquiries/2008-10/academic_freedom/hearings/091008|title=Inquiry into Academic Freedom|author=APH|date=9 September 2008|work=[[Parliament of Australia]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701104937/http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Committees/Senate/Education_Employment_and_Workplace_Relations/Completed_inquiries/2008-10/academic_freedom/hearings/091008|archive-date=1 July 2017}}</ref> The crustacean ''[[Polychelidae|Polycheles]] martini'' was named after him.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=S.|last1=Ahyong|first2=D.E.|last2=Brown|year=2002|title=New Species and New Records of Polychelidae from Australia (Crustacea Decapoda)|journal=[[The Raffles Bulletin of Zoology]]|volume=50|issue=1|pages=53–79|url=https://lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg/nus/pdf/PUBLICATION/Raffles%20Bulletin%20of%20Zoology/Past%20Volumes/RBZ%2050(1)/50rbz053-079.pdf|access-date=1 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221003530/https://lkcnhm.nus.edu.sg/nus/pdf/PUBLICATION/Raffles%20Bulletin%20of%20Zoology/Past%20Volumes/RBZ%2050(1)/50rbz053-079.pdf|archive-date=21 December 2016}}</ref>

==Biography==
Martin was born in the United States in 1947 and raised in [[Tulsa, Oklahoma]]. He earned a BA in physics at [[Rice University]] in Texas in 1969, and, seeking to avoid conscription into the [[Vietnam War]], emigrated to Australia, where he earned a PhD in physics at the [[University of Sydney]] in 1976.<ref name="Uprooting-War-104-107">{{cite book |last=Martin |first=Brian |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3yJ8QgAACAAJ |title=Uprooting War |publisher=[[Freedom Press]] |year=1984 |isbn=978-0900384264 |location=London |pages=104–107 |access-date=5 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240122093104/https://books.google.com/books?id=3yJ8QgAACAAJ |archive-date=22 January 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Martin |first=Brian |year=2021 |title=Reflections on a Life in Science and STS |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/09505431.2020.1819222 |url-status=live |journal=[[Science as Culture]] |language=en |volume=30 |issue=1 |pages=44–57 |doi=10.1080/09505431.2020.1819222 |issn= |s2cid=225193318 |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816034729/https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/09505431.2020.1819222 |archive-date=16 August 2021 |access-date=16 August 2021}}</ref>

==Research and academia==
Martin's original academic field was [[theoretical physics]], and he worked in both stratospheric modelling and numerical methods during his career. He has published extensively about the [[social dynamics]] and politicisation of controversial scientific topics. His topics of inquiry have included the globalization of polarised science such as the [[origin of HIV/AIDS]].<ref name=":1" /> He argues that there are situations in which scientific research that threatens vested interests can be suppressed. He describes a number of direct and indirect mechanisms through which he argues that this can occur, ranging from the denial of funds and the denial of promotion and tenure, through to the creation of a "general climate of fear".<ref>Hess, David J. (1997). ''Science Studies: An Advanced Introduction'', NYU Press. {{ISBN|978-0814735640}}. p152.</ref> Martin's work on in this area has provided what Delborne describes as a "key foundation for conceptualizing scientific dissent".<ref name="delborne2008" />

Martin has been active in the criticism of university systems. He has criticized conflicts of interest where universities are managing internal investigations that may lead to bad publicity, and recommends having independent groups investigate allegations of misconduct;<ref name="abc-unsw">{{cite news|last=Colvin|first=Mark|url=http://www.abc.net.au/pm/content/2014/s3988043.htm|title=PM: Investigations mounting into research at University of New South Wales|date=17 April 2014|work=PM - ABC Radio|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170513064018/http://www.abc.net.au/pm/content/2014/s3988043.htm|archive-date=13 May 2017|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation}}</ref> he has written about the unauthorised use of research produced by students and junior researchers by senior academics;<ref name="papers">{{Cite news|title=Papers retracted after authors used unauthorised data from junior researchers|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/papers-retracted-after-authors-used-unauthorised-data-from-junior-researchers|last=Matthews|first=David|date=22 October 2015|work=[[Times Higher Education]]|location=London, UK|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312083340/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/papers-retracted-after-authors-used-unauthorised-data-from-junior-researchers|archive-date=12 March 2016}}</ref> and he has been outspoken against sexual relationships between staff and students.<ref>Harvey, Sarah. (14 February 2010). "Staff-student review may have wider impact", ''[[The Sunday Star-Times]]'', New Zealand. pA005.</ref><ref>Powell, Stan. (29 May 1993). "Uni Staff Attacked for having Sex with Students", ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]'', p 11.</ref> He also reports that any bias within universities could simply be due to students strategically working in-line with the biases of their teachers.<ref name=":0" />

Martin believes that if complainants go through the official channels the outcome is very predictable, in that the organisation's internal grievance procedures, or making a complaint to the relevant ombudsman, does not work.<ref name="BBC"/> He also believes whistleblower laws do not work, saying; "Not only are whistleblower laws flawed through exemptions and in-built weaknesses but in their implementation they are rarely helpful".<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.topsecretwriters.com/2014/12/whistleblower-protection-act-really-protect/|title=Who Does The Whistleblower Protection Act Really Protect?|author=Pickard, Gabrielle|date=25 December 2014|website=Top Secret Writers|location=US|language=en-US|access-date=19 March 2016|archive-date=29 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329022043/http://www.topsecretwriters.com/2014/12/whistleblower-protection-act-really-protect/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Controversies==
{{Criticism section|date=August 2021}}

=== Academic freedom ===
Martin was subjected{{when|date=October 2025}} to an attempted [[Gag order|academic gag]] when he published material about the forced retirement of a [[University of Adelaide]] academic. His university instructed him to remove the content from his website after Adelaide University threatened to sue. Martin's published material in question is now found on other websites.<ref name="gagged">{{Cite news |last=Cervini |first=Erica |date=1 December 1999 |title=Gagged. Victoria's academics feel increasingly stifled as funding cuts force their universities down the big-business path |work=[[The Age]] |publisher=Fairfax |location=Melbourne |page=1(67)}}</ref>{{verify quote|date=October 2025}}

In April 2001, Martin published an article in defence of [[Edward J. Steele]], a sacked academic at UOW in the national newspaper ''The Australian.''<ref>{{Cite news|last=Martin|first=Brian|title=Higher Education Supplement|date=18 April 2001|work=The Australian|publisher=News Corp|url=https://theaustralian.digitaleditions.com.au/edition.php?code=NCAUS&date=2001-04-18}}{{Dead link|date=July 2022}}</ref> In a response published in the same paper, the Vice-Chancellor of [[Murdoch University]] [[Steven Schwartz (psychologist)|Steven Schwartz]] accused Martin of a position supporting the concept of a "laissez-faire attitude towards academic freedom (in which all sides are presented impartially)" saying his "approach to academic freedom is neither logical nor practical" as this approach "forces universities to abandon their most cherished values: scholarship, wisdom and truth".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cis.org.au/commentary/articles/laissez-faire-not-fair-for-all/|title=Laissez faire not fair for all|last1=Schwartz|first1=Steven|last2=Schwartz|first2=Gregory|date=27 June 2001|website=The Centre for Independent Studies|publisher=(originally published in The Australian, 27 June 2001 p.31)|location=Sydney|language=en-AU|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200109062420/https://www.cis.org.au/commentary/articles/laissez-faire-not-fair-for-all/|archive-date=9 January 2020}}</ref>

=== Vaccines ===
Martin has offered support for the discredited [[OPV AIDS hypothesis|proposal that oral polio vaccine caused AIDS]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 January 2016 |title=Debunked: The Polio Vaccine and HIV Link |url=http://www.historyofvaccines.org/content/articles/debunked-polio-vaccine-and-hiv-link |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191201135717/https://www.historyofvaccines.org/content/articles/debunked-polio-vaccine-and-hiv-link |archive-date=1 December 2019 |website=historyofvaccines.org |publisher=The College of Physicians of Philadelphia}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Hammar |first=Lawrence |date=1 April 2004 |title=Dephlogistication, Imperial Display, Apes, Angels, and the Return of Monsieur Emile Zola |journal=Papua New Guinea Medical Journal |volume=47 |issue=1–2 |pages=120, 124 |s2cid=50897742}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Martin |first=Brian |date=2010 |title=How to Attack a Scientific Theory and Get Away with It (Usually): The Attempt to Destroy an Origin-of-AIDS Hypothesis |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/share/MGGRMPZWG6MCAID6QZC2?target=10.1080/09505430903186088 |journal=Science as Culture |language=en |volume=19 |issue=2 |pages=215–239 |doi=10.1080/09505430903186088 |issn=0950-5431 |url-access=limited}}</ref> The hypothesis first came to notice in ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' magazine by way of journalist Curtis and AIDS activist Elswood in 1992, and was later further promoted by the journalist/writer Hooper and Martin,<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite magazine |author=Curtis, Tom |date=19 March 1992 |title=The Origin of AIDS: A startling new theory attempts to answer the question, 'Was it an act of God or an act of man? |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |pages=54–9, 61, 106, 108 |issue=626}}</ref> with Hooper crediting Martin for giving the OPV-AIDS link hypothesis "further publicity and credibility".<ref name="hooper-river">{{Cite book |last=Hooper |first=Edward |url=https://archive.org/details/riverjourneytoso00hoop/page/797 |title=The River: A Journey Back to the Source of HIV and AIDS |publisher=Little Brown and Company |year=1999 |isbn=0316372617 |location=US |page=[https://archive.org/details/riverjourneytoso00hoop/page/797 797] |url-access=registration}}</ref> Martin disputes the claim that he has been a supporter of the hypothesis, instead saying that he has "never argued in favour of the OPV theory", but has instead stated "that it was and remains worthy of consideration yet in many ways has been unfairly dismissed".<ref>Martin, Brian. (16 May 2016). "[https://www.bmartin.cc/dissent/documents/AIDS/Martin16.pdf Critical thinking about the origin of AIDS: Comments on Stephen Jenkins' account]". Retrieved 26 August 2016.</ref> A 2016 article in ''[[The Australian]]'' described Martin's 2010 paper as claiming "that medical researchers had colluded to silence the theory that the AIDS virus was caused by contaminated polio vaccines in 1950s Africa."<ref name="Australian-spruik" />

Immunologist and research scientist Greg Woods refuted Martin's posit on the [[Tasmanian devil facial tumour disease]] stating Martin's 2014 paper in [[The Conversation (website)|''The Conversation'']] on the theory behind the cancer "misrepresents the state of the science".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theconversation.com/tassie-devil-facial-tumour-is-a-transmissible-cancer-34312|title=Tassie devil facial tumour is a transmissible cancer|last=Woods|first=Greg|date=18 November 2014|website=theconversation.edu.au|publisher=The Conversation Media Group Ltd|location=Parkville, Vic.|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412071359/http://theconversation.com/tassie-devil-facial-tumour-is-a-transmissible-cancer-34312|archive-date=12 April 2019|edition=Australian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://theconversation.com/whats-killing-tassie-devils-if-it-isnt-a-contagious-cancer-32318|title=What's killing Tassie devils if it isn't a contagious cancer?|last1=Martin|first1=Brian|last2=Warren|first2=Jody|date=16 November 2014|website=theconversation.edu.au|publisher=The Conversation Media Group Ltd|location=Parkville, Vic.|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413044552/http://theconversation.com/whats-killing-tassie-devils-if-it-isnt-a-contagious-cancer-32318|archive-date=13 April 2019|edition=Australian}}</ref>{{Relevance inline|discuss=Is this relevant to his biography or just a blip given undue weight?|date=August 2021}}

In 2014, Martin published a paper characterising criticism of [[Andrew Wakefield]]'s [[Lancet MMR autism fraud|discredited claims about vaccines and autism]] as "suppression of vaccination dissent".<ref name="suppression">{{cite journal|last=Martin|first=Brian|title=On the Suppression of Vaccination Dissent|journal=[[Science and Engineering Ethics]]|date=2015|volume=21|issue=1|pages=143–157|doi=10.1007/s11948-014-9530-3|pmid=24658876|s2cid=9824788|url=https://ro.uow.edu.au/lhapapers/1883|access-date=4 January 2020|archive-date=4 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200104162047/https://ro.uow.edu.au/lhapapers/1883/|url-status=live}} Published online: 23 March 2014.</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=August 2021}} In 2016, an Agence Science-Presse piece accused Martin of defending "the idea of a vaccine-autism link."<ref name="Lapointe">{{Cite news|title=L'anti-vaccination à l'université|url=https://www.sciencepresse.qc.ca/actualite/2016/01/15/lanti-vaccination-luniversite|last=Lapointe|first=Pascal|date=15 January 2016|work=[[:fr:Agence Science-Presse|Agence Science Presse]]|location=Quebec, CA.|language=fr|trans-title=Anti-vaccination at university|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226031011/http://www.sciencepresse.qc.ca/actualite/2016/01/15/lanti-vaccination-luniversite|archive-date=26 February 2016|quote=The professor she chose as supervisor, Brian Martin, is known for his belief in a conspiracy to silence and hide the study that the AIDS virus was caused by the polio vaccine. And he also defends the idea of a vaccine-autism link.}}</ref> However, Martin disputes this, saying: "I have never defended this idea."<ref name=WikipediaBias>{{cite journal|last=Martin|first=Brian|year=2018|title=Persistent Bias on Wikipedia: Methods and Responses|journal=[[Social Science Computer Review]]|volume=36|issue=3|pages=379–388|doi=10.1177/0894439317715434|s2cid=65125326}}</ref> ''[[The Australian]]'' reported that "Martin is a former paid member of the anti-vaccine [[Australian Vaccination Network]]", and that Martin states that he is also a member of the American [[Skeptics Society]].<ref name="australian-conference"/>

Martin has been criticised for his role in the [[Judith Wilyman PhD controversy]] where medical academics and the [[Australian Medical Association|AMA]] raised concerns of whether Martin had the necessary knowledge to assess her doctorate which discussed [[vaccine]] science.<ref name="Australian-spruik">{{Cite In 2016, the [[Australian Skeptics]] criticised Martin's supervision of Wilyman by presenting Martin, Wilyman and the Social Sciences Department of the University of Wollongong the satirical [[Bent Spoon Award]] for awarding "a PhD thesis riddled with errors, misstatements, poor and unsupported 'evidence' and conspiratorial thinking".<ref>{{cite web|title=2016 Skeptics awards – Spoon to Wilyman, Skeptic of the Year to Harvey and Vickers|url=http://www.skeptics.com.au/2016/11/28/2016-skeptics-awards-spoon-to-wilyman-skeptic-of-the-year-to-harvey-and-vickers/|date=28 November 2016|website=Australian Skeptics|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318074510/https://www.skeptics.com.au/2016/11/28/2016-skeptics-awards-spoon-to-wilyman-skeptic-of-the-year-to-harvey-and-vickers/|archive-date=18 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Skeptics name winners of Bent Spoon award|url=http://www.pharmacynews.com.au/News/Skeptics-name-winners-of-Bent-Spoon-award|date=28 November 2016|work=Pharmacy News|publisher=Australian Doctor Group|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161129082741/http://www.pharmacynews.com.au/News/Skeptics-name-winners-of-Bent-Spoon-award|archive-date=29 November 2016}}</ref>
